Subject: Fleet sizing and contingency for reserved capacity commit — OmniHealth

Hi Alice,

Thanks again for the time earlier — excited about the potential to support OmniHealth's inference workload for clinical summarization. Attached is an initial sizing that maps the committed throughput in DEAL-8742 to expected GPU pools (omni_capacity_plan_v1.xlsx).

Two items I wanted to flag up-front so we can be explicit in the contract:
- Sizing window: this plan assumes a 24-month commit with quarterly reviews; it uses conservative utilization (45%) for latency SLOs.
- Price sensitivity: we expect GPU spot and list prices to move materially over the next 12–24 months. We can offer a tiered discount tied to committed volume, but OmniHealth asked about a mechanism to protect you if GPU input costs spike.

Proposed next steps: please review the capacity plan. If you confirm the target throughput ranges, we'll propose a contract appendix with two options — (A) fixed discount schedule by SKUs, or (B) a price-contingency clause that triggers additional discount/credits if market GPU list rates rise above a defined index.

I've cc'd Procurement so we can keep traceability. Attaching: omni_capacity_plan_v1.xlsx and a draft term sheet summary.

Cheers,
Jonas

Jonas — thanks for the plan. A few quick points from our side:

1) We like option B (price-contingency) but need clarity on the trigger and math. Our procurement lead wants a simple index (e.g., public GPU list rate or a published cloud GPU index) and a floor so Redwood doesn't pass through small fluctuations.

2) If the contingency reduces effective unit price for us, we need to understand how that flows through billing and whether it reduces committed capacity (we prefer credits rather than reshaping capacity).

3) Approval path: Anything that materially increases our vendor credit exposure or changes effective discount >20% will need board sign-off.

Can you put together a short worked example showing 3 scenarios (base, +20% GPU market shock, +50% shock) with the impact to our per-token economics? 

Best,
Alice

- They want a simple public index trigger and a floor that avoids passing small noise.
- Anything that creates effective discount >20% requires their board sign-off. Our approval matrix: what discount level requires VP/CEO approval? Finance: can you run the sensitivity model attached (gpu_price_sensitivity_model.xlsx) against the omni_capacity_plan_v1?

Specific questions:

2) Can we craft a clause that limits reserve exposure (e.g., cap credit liability to X% of committed spend over the prior quarter)?
3) Legal: are there standard fallback language templates for indexation triggers?

Thanks — this is time-sensitive, OmniHealth wants to close by end of May.

—Jonas

Jonas — thanks for looping us in. I ran an initial commercial framing and attached a redlined term sheet (redwood_term_sheet_v3.pdf) plus a simple worked example in gpu_price_sensitivity_model.xlsx. Summary:

- Option 1 (Tiered Discount): standard volume tiers (5%, 12%, 20%) by committed vCPU-equivalent. No indexation.
- Option 2 (Indexed Contingency): baseline discount of 10% + contingency credits when the GPU index increases > 18% vs. baseline. Credits are applied as bill credits (not capacity reduction). Credits capped at 30% of quarterly committed spend.
- Escalation/Approval: discounts up to 15% are approvable by Sales + Finance. Discounts between 15–30% require VP of Sales + Head of Finance sign-off. Anything >30% needs CEO approval and legal review.

Questions for Finance (Karthik): are we comfortable with the 30% quarterly cap? Also, what's our worst-case cash impact if the market spikes 50% for two consecutive quarters?

If Finance greenlights the cap, I suggest we present Option 2 with the cap and a simple example to Alice showing: base, +20% shock (credit = X), +50% shock (credit capped at Y).

—Marissa

Subject: Re: Fwd: Fleet sizing and contingency for reserved capacity commit — OmniHealth

Team — ran the sensitivity against the sizing plan. High-level takeaways:

1) Worst-case (50% market shock sustained 2 quarters): cash-credit exposure ≈ 18% of committed spend over that 2-quarter period (if we apply the linear credit formula). With Marissa's proposed 30% quarterly cap we reduce that exposure to ~12% because the cap prevents unbounded credits on the largest SKU tiers.

2) Recommendation: accept Option 2 (Indexed Contingency) with the following guardrails:
   - Trigger: 20% increase in the agreed public GPU index vs. baseline rolling 60-day average.
   - Floor: no credits for moves <8% to avoid passing noise.
   - Cap: quarterly credit ceiling at 30% of committed spend (this is a hard cap).
   - Rollover: unused credit does not reduce committed capacity; credits apply to future invoices only (no retroactive change to capacity).

3) Approval matrix: discounts up to 18%: Sales + Finance. 18–30%: require VP Finance sign-off and Head of Sales. >30%: exec (CEO) approval and legal concurrence.

If we go with these guardrails I think we can present a clean doc to OmniHealth. Anything that increases the cap or lowers the floor materially increases our tail risk and requires exec sign-off.

—Karthik

Date: 2028-05-10T15:38:00-07:00
Subject: Proposed contingency structure & next steps (DocuSign link)

Alice — thanks for the patience. Per our internal reviews we've drafted a clean contingency approach we think balances predictability for OmniHealth and bounded risk for Redwood. Summary (see attached term sheet and model):

- Mechanism: Indexed Contingency (Option 2) — baseline discount 10%, contingency credits if agreed public GPU index > baseline by >=20%.
- Noise floor: no credits for index moves <8%.
- Cap: quarterly credit ceiling = 30% of committed spend. Credits are off-invoice credits applied to future invoices; they do not reduce reserved capacity.
- Approval/Authority: Sales + Finance can sign up to 18% effective discount. Anything that pushes credits to create an effective discount >18% requires VP Finance sign-off (Karthik). >30% requires exec approval.

I attached the worked examples you asked for (base / +20% / +50%) in gpu_price_sensitivity_model.xlsx and the redlined term sheet. If this structure aligns with OmniHealth, please reply confirming you want us to generate a legal appendix and we'll send it for e-signature. Alternatively, if you prefer a different index or a different cap, let us know and we can re-run the math.

DocuSign (prelim): https://www.docusign.com/sign?d=8f3a-omni-deal
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/8742

If we get a thumbs up this week, Legal can turn the appendix around in 3 business days and Finance will prepare the revenue recognition memo.

Thanks,
